decisive_spans.text: a 1.5-cm diameter, exophytic, smooth, regular, and soft lesion on the midline of the dorsal tongue
the lesion had been present since birth and had not changed in size or character
the lesion appeared partly fatty, likely submucosal, demonstrated mild contrast enhancement, had intact overlying mucosa, and showed no involvement of intrinsic tongue muscles

response.rationale: The vignette describes a congenital, stable, exophytic, smooth, regular, soft, partly fatty, submucosal lesion on the midline of the dorsal tongue with mild contrast enhancement and intact overlying mucosa. Congenital Lingual Hamartoma (D1) aligns perfectly with all these characteristics. Lipoma of the Tongue (D2) is a strong contender due to the fatty appearance and submucosal location, but hamartoma is a broader term that encompasses the other features like being congenital and stable. Teratoma (D3) and Congenital Granular Cell Tumor (D4) are less specific and do not fully capture the described characteristics as well as D1.
